q-3710.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14164468/assets/663096ab9ecc1daca22587d94526cbf0db841602ca0b64eaa1a9477ec8a35aee.png)

What is the length of $a$ in the triangle shown above?
q-3710.worked_solution:
Here, we know the lengths of the hypotenuse and one leg, so let $b=12$ and $c=13.$ We need to find $a,$ the length of the other leg.

According to the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}^{2} & ={a}^{2}+{b}^{2} \\ {a}^{2} & ={c}^{2}-{b}^{2} \\ a & =\sqrt{{c}^{2}-{b}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in the values for $b$ and $c$ gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\sqrt{(13)^{2}-(12)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169-144} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the length of $a$ in the triangle shown above?
q-5650.worked_solution:
Here, we know the lengths of the hypotenuse and one leg, so let $b=\frac{15}{2}$ and $c=\frac{39}{2}.$ We need to find $a,$ the length of the other leg.

According to the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}^{2} & ={a}^{2}+{b}^{2} \\ {a}^{2} & ={c}^{2}-{b}^{2} \\ a & =\sqrt{{c}^{2}-{b}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in the values for $b$ and $c$ gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\sqrt{{(\frac{39}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{15}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1\,521}{4}-\frac{225}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{324} \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

q-82392.name: Question 3
q-82392.problem: A right triangle has legs of length $4$ and $8.$ Calculate the length of its hypotenuse.
q-82392.worked_solution:
Let $a=4,$ $b=8,$ and $c$ be the length of the hypotenuse. According to the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}^{2} & ={a}^{2}+{b}^{2} \\ c & =\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in the values for $a$ and $b$ gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\sqrt{(4)^{2}+(8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+64} \\  & =\sqrt{80} \\  & =4\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

A right triangle has legs of length 4 and 8. Calculate the length of its hypotenuse.

a
10
b
45
c
210
d
72
e
12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let a=4, b=8, and c be the length of the hypotenuse. According to the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain c2=a2+b2c=a2+b2.

Substituting in the values for a and b gives us c=(4)2+(8)2=16+64=80=45.
